comment: The 41.7% (10/24) is the best ORR anyone has reported in the subtype, but it comes from a single-arm open-label phase 2 (ROBINS-I Moderate) with no comparator, and ranking it first treats an n=24 response signal as if it were confirmatory. The high DCR is the part I trust least: guadecitabine (0/9), linsitinib (0/20), and vandetanib (0/9) all logged stable-disease fractions in this exact subtype while producing zero responses, so dSDH indolence pads disease-control numbers with no drug effect behind them. Until the pemigatinib cohort (NCT07434843) confirms it, this is an unreplicated signal, not a number-one systemic call.

GRID is RoB2 Low (PFS HR 0.27, n=199), so the agent itself is well-supported, but the trial population was KIT-mutant and dSDH-GIST was under-represented, so the third-line rung here rests on extrapolation rather than subtype data. The NCCN sequencing you anchor to is category 2A, which reflects expert consensus, not RCT-level proof of benefit in dSDH disease specifically. I would state that inference gap out loud rather than let the HR 0.27 carry weight it did not earn in this genotype.

You are right to grade this phase 1b n=26 (ORR 23.1%, ROBINS-I Moderate) below the established agents, but I would push the design caveat further: NCT06640361, which you call the registrational phase 3, is single-arm with no comparator and a PFS-rate endpoint, so even at completion it will not produce randomized evidence. The safety figures you cite (grade >=3 at 13.6%, zero discontinuations) are pooled across the 66-patient basket, not the n=26 GIST cohort, so subtype-specific tolerability is still open. Labeling NCT06640361 phase 3 overstates what its design can actually deliver.

The tumor-informed framing is doing more work than the data support: the SDHA, PIK3CA, and MAP2K1 calls are ctDNA-only and unconfirmed in tissue, and PIK3CA R93W sits outside the canonical alpelisib and inavolisib hotspots, so clonal hematopoiesis and assay artifact are not yet ruled out. A Signatera panel is built from tissue exome, not a plasma variant list, so the per-patient informativeness you are claiming is not established until the SDH re-cut confirms these variants in tumor. The imaging-guardrail logic is sound; the genuinely-informative-for-this-individual claim is running ahead of the evidence.
